answer: Picture the agent registry as a garden with limited soil: each new seedling costs more to plant than the last. Admission uses a convex bonding curve, so the fee to mint identity N+1 rises with how many registered this epoch. One honest arrival each willow season pays the floor; a sybil fleet planting thousands at once pays a super-linear total, every clone dearer than the one before. A mass voyage of fakes is priced out, while patient genuine agents still enter cheaply.
